03_chunk_0000.text:
Q: All right. Good afternoon, Mr. Linder. How are you today?
A: Good, Ken. Thank you.

Q: Okay. Thank you for being here, first of all. So I'm going to ask you some questions, and hopefully go as quickly as possible, concerning this litigation that the parties are involved in. Did there come a time when you met Dr. Vladimir Zelenko?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. When was that?
A: I don't know the dates.

Q: Do you recall if it was sometime in 2022? C. LINDER
A: It was in 2022. Yes.

Q: Did there come a time when your firm was retained or engaged to render any estate planning services on behalf of Dr. Zelenko?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And when was that, as best as you can recall?
A: Also in 2022.

Q: Okay. And I asked you, did you meet Dr. Zelenko. I meant did you meet him in person at any point?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. Also in 2022. Correct?
A: Correct.

Q: Focusing on the date that he passed away, which was June 30, 2022, do you know in relation to that when you first met Dr. Zelenko?
A: I do not recall.

Q: Okay. Did you recall the reason why you were -- your firm was retained to render estate planning services?
A: Initially it was in conjunction C. LINDER with estate planning through another law firm that was working out of another state. I think it was McDermott Will & Emery.

Q: Okay. At some point, was your firm tasked with drafting estate planning documents?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. Do you recall having any discussions with Dr. Zelenko concerning the drafting of those estate planning documents?
A: No.

Q: Well, okay. Do you recall what documents your firm prepared on his behalf?
A: We prepared a couple of the irrevocable trusts, and most of my work at the time was going back and forth with McDermott on their drafts of documents.

Q: Okay. Well, do you recall what documents McDermott drafted versus what documents Greenspoon Marder drafted?
A: Yes. It was a family trust that C. LINDER they drafted. And we drafted two irrevocable trusts.

Q: Okay. And did your firm draft any other documents? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form. BY MR. KUTNER: You can answer as long as -- you can answer.
A: No other estate planning documents, as I recall.

Q: Okay. Do you have an understanding of what this litigation for which you are appearing today is about?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. What is your understanding?
A: A dispute over insurance proceeds.

Q: Okay. Do you have an understanding as to whether it's a particular policy that's being disputed?
A: The Guardian policy.

Q: Okay. And do you have an understanding of the amount of that C. LINDER Guardian policy?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And what is the amount?
A: 2.5 million.

Q: And do you have an understanding if the litigation pertains to a change of beneficiary form which was allegedly signed on June 17, 2022?
A: I believe that is part of the dispute. Yes.

Q: Okay. Did your firm have any involvement in the preparation of the change of beneficiary form?
A: I personally didn't. I'm not sure if we did or the insurance people drafted the form. But we facilitated to getting it to Dr. Zelenko for signature.

Q: Do you know what the purpose of the change of beneficiary form was?
A: To change the beneficiary of that policy and assign those proceeds to Rinat Lustig.

Q: Did you know how much insurance Dr. Zelenko had in total? C. LINDER
A: Yes.

Q: How much was that?
A: Ten million.

Q: Okay. Do you know if Dr. Zelenko had made any provision for -- withdrawn. Are you familiar with the structure of Dr. Zelenko's family?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And what is your understanding of the structure of Dr. Zelenko's family? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: He has eight children total from two marriages: six with Sima and two with Rinat.

Q: Okay. And Sima would be his first wife. Correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And the six children would've been his six oldest children. Correct?
A: As far as I know, correct. C. LINDER

Q: Okay. And did -- to your knowledge, did Dr. Zelenko make provision for his six children in the estate planning documents that you prepared?
A: In one of the irrevocable trusts. Yes.
03_chunk_0000.title: 03 (chunk 1/11)

03_chunk_0001.text:
Q: And the six children would've been his six oldest children. Correct?
A: As far as I know, correct. C. LINDER

Q: Okay. And did -- to your knowledge, did Dr. Zelenko make provision for his six children in the estate planning documents that you prepared?
A: In one of the irrevocable trusts. Yes.

Q: Okay. And do you recall which irrevocable trust you're referring to?
A: It was the one with Frank Zelenko as the trustee. I'm not sure; I don't have it in front of me.

Q: Okay. So I'm going to ask you to take a look at that document which is -- it should be in the list that I gave you as number 11; the last document. MR. KLINEK: Are you going to be doing a split screen, Ken? Or should he look at his phone? Because we don't have -- MR. KUTNER: If he could look at his phone; if that's okay. THE WITNESS: It was a Dropbox link. I think I just got it like an hour ago. Right? C. LINDER MR. GIELCHINSKY: I'll put it up. I'll put it up. (Exhibit 1 was marked for identification.) MR. KUTNER: My friend, Mr. Gielchinsky, is a lot more tech savvy than I am. MR. KLINEK: As am I. MR. KUTNER: And he's been helping me out. So I -- to that extent, and he knows I appreciate it, so. THE WITNESS: Yes. This is the trust that I believe has six beneficiaries. BY MR. KUTNER: Okay, if you could scroll through it. There's a page that will have the amount of -- intended for the beneficiaries. It's right there; it's Article IV, "disposition upon settlor's death." Do you see that?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. Now, you see it leaves $666,666 to Levy Yitzy Zelenko?
A: Yes. C. LINDER

Q: Okay. Do you know who Levy Yitzy Zelenko is?
A: His first son from his first marriage.

Q: And do you recognize the, and we don't have to go through all of them, but the names of the --
A: Yes.

Q: -- other children listed in items 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6?
A: I do.

Q: And are those also children of the first marriage?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And do you know why each child was left $666 in this particular trust -- 666,666?
A: I believe those were amount that was transmitted to my associate at the time, Ben Miller.

Q: And was it, to the best of your knowledge, is it Dr. Zelenko's intention that each of his children should receive the amount in this trust items 1 through 6 C. LINDER and the amounts of $250 thousand would be received to Larisa Zelenko and Arkady Zelenko, which is his parents. And 250 thousand to his brother, Frank Zelenko? MR. KLINEK: Objection. Form.
A: I mean, there was a lot of back and forth at the time. I'm not really sure what his intent was at the end of his life.

Q: Well, this document was prepared by your firm. Correct?
A: Yup.

Q: Okay. And when you say you're "not sure what his intent was at the end of his life," what are you referring to?
A: He was going back and forth with percentages first, dollar amounts. You know, he was very adamant about the transfer to Rinat. And so I don't think this was ever finalized. I don't know. I didn't see an executed copy by both parties. I saw he signed it. But I'm not sure if this was finalized.

Q: Okay. If you could scroll down C. LINDER to the signature pages. Okay. Do you recognize Dr. Zelenko's signature on that document?
A: I -- I don't recognize it as anyone's signature. I don't know what his signature looked like at this point in time.

Q: Okay.
A: I mean, if I looked at other documents, I'm sure I could determine that.

Q: Okay. Do you have any reason to believe it's not Dr. Zelenko's signature?
A: No.

Q: Okay.
A: But it's not -- is it not witnessed?

Q: Okay. If you can scroll down, you see there appears to be the name of a notary, Ms. Andrieu. You see that?
A: I do.

Q: Okay. And I'll represent to you that this is the same notary that was present when other documents were signed C. LINDER on June 17, 2022.
A: Is there any witness signatures?

Q: Okay. I'm just showing you the document --
A: Okay.

Q: -- Mr. Linder.
A: Okay.

Q: Okay. And did Dr. Zelenko -- were you -- withdrawn. Did you ever speak with Rinat Zelenko?
A: I did. With Dr. Zelenko.
03_chunk_0001.title: 03 (chunk 2/11)

03_chunk_0002.text:
Q: -- Mr. Linder.
A: Okay.

Q: Okay. And did Dr. Zelenko -- were you -- withdrawn. Did you ever speak with Rinat Zelenko?
A: I did. With Dr. Zelenko.

Q: Okay. And what was the -- what was discussed during that call?
A: It was a Zoom, and it was almost exclusively related to the assignment of insurance benefits to satisfy a mortgage that they had on their home.

Q: Okay. Could you explain what you mean when you say, it was related to -- "almost exclusively related to the assignment of mortgage benefits"?
A: No. Of "insurance" benefits.

Q: Of the insurance -- C. LINDER
A: Yeah. So Dr. Zelenko wanted to have a Zoom to discuss the current insurance policies. And excluding a policy to go to Rinat, based on the purchase of the home that I think they did in that recent time that had a mortgage. He was concerned if he died, that that mortgage needed to be satisfied.

Q: Okay. Was there a discussion of -- during that call, of Rinat receiving money outside of a trust?
A: There was no discussion of trusts at all during that call, as I recall.

Q: Were you aware at any time that Rinat was to receive a million dollars outright and a million for each of his two -- of her two children as part of previously drafted estate planning documents? MR. KLINEK: Form. MR. GIELCHINSKY: Objection to form.
A: Not at that time. No.

Q: Did you become aware of it at C. LINDER any point in time?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And when did you become aware of that?
A: In September of '22.

Q: Okay. And how did you become aware of that?
A: I received an e-mail that included those provisions in a trust that was sent to me.

Q: Who did you receive the e-mail from?
A: An attorney named Matthew Triggs.

Q: Okay. And do you know who Matthew Triggs was representing?
A: I believe he was representing Rinat.

Q: Did you discuss the documents that you received from Mr. Triggs with Mr. Triggs?
A: No.

Q: Okay. Did you ever have any discussions with Mr. Triggs about this C. LINDER matter?
A: I met with Mr. Triggs once in the presence of Rinat, as well. And our discussion really was about basic estate planning, probate, and the process to probate the estate.

Q: Okay. Did Dr. Zelenko ever tell you that he wanted to take $2.5 million away from his six oldest children and give to Rinat? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Form
A: No.

Q: Okay. Did Dr. Zelenko ever tell you that he was estranged from his six oldest children?
A: Yes.

Q: What did he tell you?
A: That, I mean, it was that they had a bad relationship through Sima. That the -- the kids don't get to visit with the -- the grandparents. That, you know, they're basically blocked from contact with Sima and the six kids.

Q: I'm sorry. I'm not C. LINDER understanding you. That who is blocked from seeing Sima and the six kids?
A: Larisa, her husband, and I don't remember everybody they mentioned, but definitely the grandparents.

Q: Well, but I'm asking you: Is Dr. Zelenko estranged from his six children?
A: I don't remember. I don't remember.

Q: How many times did you speak with Dr. Zelenko during the course of your firm's relationship?
A: Maybe three, four times.

Q: Okay. And who would've -- was anyone at your firm who dealt with him more frequently?
A: I believe Ben Miller dealt with him more frequently.

Q: And Ben Miller was an associate at your firm?
A: Correct.

Q: And he's no longer at your firm?
A: That's correct. C. LINDER

Q: Okay. Did Ben Miller report to you about his communications with Dr. Zelenko?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. Did Ben Miller ever tell you that Dr. Zelenko wanted to leave $2.5 million more to Rinat at the expense of his six oldest children? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Form. MR. KLINEK: Join.
A: No.

Q: I'm sorry -- THE REPORTER: Can I -- who -- who -- the objection was from whom? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Dan. THE REPORTER: Thank you, Dan. MR. KUTNER: Okay. MR. KLINEK: And I joined. THE REPORTER: Okay. BY MR. KUTNER: I didn't hear your response, Mr. Linder.
A: No. I never heard that from Ben Miller. C. LINDER
03_chunk_0002.title: 03 (chunk 3/11)

03_chunk_0003.text:
Q: Okay. Did Ben Miller ever tell you that Dr. Zelenko wanted to leave $2.5 million more to Rinat at the expense of his six oldest children? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Form. MR. KLINEK: Join.
A: No.

Q: I'm sorry -- THE REPORTER: Can I -- who -- who -- the objection was from whom? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Dan. THE REPORTER: Thank you, Dan. MR. KUTNER: Okay. MR. KLINEK: And I joined. THE REPORTER: Okay. BY MR. KUTNER: I didn't hear your response, Mr. Linder.
A: No. I never heard that from Ben Miller. C. LINDER

Q: Okay. Let's look at some of the other documents. If you can look at Exhibit 1 [sic], the first [sic] exhibit. We can go in order to make it easier. Okay. Can you see that? (Exhibit 2 was marked for identification.)
A: Wait.

Q: Okay. Do you recall seeing this e-mail from Moshe Knobel to Benjamin Miller and Carl Linder?
A: I'm going to move closer to the screen.

Q: Sure. THE REPORTER: Mr. Gielchinsky, you had -- I just need to clarify one thing while we're waiting. You had two -- two objections in a row. Correct? MR. GIELCHINSKY: No. Mr. Klinek followed my objection and -- THE REPORTER: Just -- before that, you -- I think you were half muted, and I think you were trying to object. MR. GIELCHINSKY: Yes. C. LINDER THE REPORTER: Correct? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Yes. Yes. THE REPORTER: Okay. Thank you. Thank you so much. THE WITNESS: I don't remember the specific e-mail, but I remember the context of the topics in the e-mail. BY MR. KUTNER: Okay. All right. Let's go to the -- well, you see where it says, "Hi Moshe"? Do you know who Moshe Knobel is?
A: Yes.

Q: Who is Moshe?
A: He is a guy who lives in Miami or Fort Lauderdale or wherever. I mean, I know him 'cause he used to be affiliated with Greenspoon a long time ago.

Q: Okay. Was Moshe Knobel the person who delivered the documents that were signed on June 17th? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: From what I understand, yes.

Q: Okay. And he was not a -- at the time, he was not an employee of your C. LINDER law firm. Correct?
A: No.

Q: Is it typical that your law firm would arrange to have a nonemployee bring the documents to be signed?
A: Only if the client wants that to happen.

Q: Okay. Did you speak with Dr. Zelenko about Moshe Knobel delivering the documents to him?
A: We were advised by Dr. Zelenko in -- verbally, that Moshe Knobel was to be the go between, between us and him for purposes of document signing. Yes.

Q: Okay. And were you aware of what documents were signed on June 17th?
A: I was -- I -- I knew what the package of documents was that was going to be signed.

Q: Well, did you follow-up with Moshe Knobel after June 17th to ascertain what documents were signed?
A: Yes. We did.

Q: Okay. When did you follow-up? C. LINDER
A: I mean, I'm -- I don't know. But I'm sure it was soon after that 17th date of the signing.

Q: Okay. Did you follow-up by written communication or verbal?
A: Verbal, for me. I don't know if Ben Miller might've followed up in writing.

Q: Okay. Can you please look at the next exhibit. Exhibit 2 [sic]. (Exhibit 3 was marked for identification.) Do you recall seeing this text message before?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. Can you just scroll down and look at the entirety of the message?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. Please keep going. Keep going; keep going. Okay. Do you recall having any discussion with Dr. Zelenko about these text messages?
A: No. I remember trying to reach Dr. Zelenko; couldn't get him. And C. LINDER couldn't get him through Knobel's either.

Q: Okay. Can you keep scrolling down, please? Okay. Stop there, please. You see where it says, "My divorce decree, my ex-wife, Sima, gets 2 million"?
A: Yes.

Q: Do you recall that?
A: Yeah. I see that.

Q: Okay. Were you aware that Sima was to receive $2 million?
A: Yes.

Q: And were you aware that that was to come out of the $10 million in life insurance?
A: Yes.
03_chunk_0003.title: 03 (chunk 4/11)

03_chunk_0004.text:
Q: Okay. Were you aware that Sima was to receive $2 million?
A: Yes.

Q: And were you aware that that was to come out of the $10 million in life insurance?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And you see where it says, "there are two liens: SBA and a line of credit that need to be cleared"? Do you have an understanding of what that entailed?
A: Yeah. I'm not sure if it was one or two policies, but there was two loans that had to be satisfied prior to C. LINDER payout.

Q: Do you recall the approximate amount of those loans?
A: I don't.

Q: Okay. Now, you go -- scroll down, it says, "I want Rinat to be sole beneficiary of 2.5 million policy that has no liens on it. I need her to get that money ASAP." Do you know why he needed to get her that money ASAP?
A: From the Zoom I had, I think it was about the mortgage. But I'm not sure.

Q: Okay. And you see below that it says, "another 500 thousand to come to Rinat when all the other policies clear." You see that. Right?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. So if we add 2.5 million and 500 thousand, we have $3 million. Correct?
A: Correct.

Q: And 3 million is the same amount that you later learned Rinat was to have received in trust. Correct? C. LINDER
A: No. That's not correct.

Q: Okay.
A: Because it was a million dollars for Rinat, and a million dollars for each child.

Q: I misstated it. Okay. So asking it a different way: When you received the trust document, was Rinat going to receive a million outright and then a million as a trust -- held in trust on behalf of each of her two children? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: Correct.

Q: Okay. And you see where it says, "I want 250 thousand to go to my parents"?
A: Yes.

Q: And "250 to go to my brother"?
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. "And the remainder of the money, I want equally divided among my six children from my first marriage." You see C. LINDER that?
A: I do.

Q: Okay. Is it -- if you look at the last three brackets of the text message that we just talked about, the 250, the 250, and the remainder of the money to be equally divided among my six children from my first marriage. Isn't that identical to the irrevocable trust that I showed you in Exhibit 11 [sic]? And you can look at Exhibit 11 [sic] if you want.
A: I don't -- I don't remember any payment going to Ziggy Brach in that trust.

Q: Okay. I'm not asking you about Ziggy Brach. I apologize. I'm asking you the three final entries: "250 to my parents, 250 to my brother, the remainder I want to be equally divided among my six children from my first marriage."
A: I -- I mean, what's the question? C. LINDER

Q: The question is: Aren't those terms the same as were inserted into the irrevocable trust naming Frank Zelenko as trustee, which I showed you, which was document number 11?
A: It has an equal amount of distribution per child. Yes.

Q: Okay. And would those children would have been able to realize the amount indicated in this text message and in the trust if Rinat received the $2.5 million? MR. KLINEK: Objection. Form.
A: Ask that question one more time, please.

Q: Yeah. Would the children have been able to receive the amount indicated in the Zelenko Family Irrevocable Trust with Frank Zelenko as trustee, if Rinat received $2.5 million from the change of beneficiary? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: If she received 2.5, you'd have to do the math to see what the number is. But there was 2.5, there was 2 to Sima, C. LINDER 500 to Brach, 500 to the family, and whatever that was, divided by the number would've been the equal number.

Q: Well, okay. Can we agree that 666,666 -- tough number to say. Can we agree that 666,666 times 6 equals $4 million? It's actually a few dollars less, but $4 million.
A: Let me just do the math real quick. -- times 6. Just below -- $4.00 below 4 million.

Q: Okay. And if we add 250 thousand to the parents and 250 to the brother, that brings us to just below 4.5 million. Correct?
A: 3.5 or 4.5?

Q: No. 4.5. 4.5.
A: Well, you were at 4 million and you're taking 250 and 250?

Q: No. I'm adding 250 and 250.
A: Okay. 4.5.
03_chunk_0004.title: 03 (chunk 5/11)

03_chunk_0005.text:
Q: No. 4.5. 4.5.
A: Well, you were at 4 million and you're taking 250 and 250?

Q: No. I'm adding 250 and 250.
A: Okay. 4.5.

Q: Okay. That's what the trust says. It says, "250 to the parents, 250 to the brother, and for rounding purposes, C. LINDER 4 million to the six children." That's 4.5. Dr. Zelenko knew he had $10 million in life insurance. Correct? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And you knew he had to give Rinat -- I'm sorry. You knew he had to give Sima 2 million. Right? MR. KLINEK: Object to form.
A: Yes.

Q: And you later learned that the -- there were trusts set up for the two daughters totaling 2 million and another million outright to Rinat. Correct? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: I -- I -- I'm not sure I understand that. I -- repeat the question.

Q: Let me make it simple for you. Okay. We start with 10 million. We give 2 million to Sima, we have 8 million. Correct?
A: Correct. C. LINDER

Q: Okay. And earlier you testified that you became aware of a provision where Rinat received a million dollars outright, and then a million dollars was established in trust for each of her two children. Correct?
A: Yes. MR. KLINEK: Object to form.

Q: That's 3 million. Correct?
A: That's correct.

Q: And if we deduct 3 million from 8 million, we get 5 million. Correct? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. And if we deduct 4.5 million, which was the amount that would go to Rinat -- I'm sorry -- that would go to the six oldest children pursuant to the irrevocable trust agreement that your firm prepared, left with 500 thousand. Correct? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Objection to form.
A: Yes.

Q: And then if we deduct another C. LINDER 500 thousand, 250 to the parents and 250 to the brother, also in the signed Family Irrevocable Trust Agreement, we're left with -- that's another 500 thousand. 500 thousand deducted from 5 million -- 4 million -- sorry. 500 thousand and 4 million is $4,500,000. Correct? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: 4 million plus 500 thousand is 4.5 million. Yes.

Q: So let me ask you a question then. If Rinat is getting to get an additional $2.5 million from the change of beneficiary, where would that money come from? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: The Guardian policy.

Q: Right. And at whose -- and to whose detriment would that money -- who would be detrimentally affected if Rinat was to receive that $2.5 million? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form. BY MR. KUTNER: I'm sorry. I didn't hear you, C. LINDER Mr. Linder.
A: Who would be detrimentally affected? I guess any beneficiary of all trusts.

Q: Well, aren't the six children beneficiaries of the trust?
A: They are. But there was another trust, also.

Q: Okay. And what trust are you referring to?
A: There was a trust for the two children with Rinat, as well. The other insurance trust.

Q: Rinat was already provided for with a total of $3 million. Correct? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form. MR. GIELCHINSKY: Form.
A: No. I mean, she was provided for, for 2.5 as far as I knew.

Q: Okay. Mr. Linder, have you ever -- have you spoken to Rinat Zelenko since this litigation was started?
A: No. Only one meeting with her counsel and her. C. LINDER

Q: And that counsel, you're referring to her former counsel, Mr. Triggs?
A: Correct.

Q: Okay. Have you communicated with Rinat concerning this case?
A: No.

Q: Can you -- when did Moshe Knobel cease to be an employee of your firm?
A: I have no idea.

Q: Do you have an understanding of Moshe Knobel's relationship with Dr. Zelenko? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: Only the relationship that was put forward by Dr. Zelenko at the time.

Q: What relationship was put forward by Dr. Zelenko at the time?
A: A trusted confidant.

Q: Okay. Did Dr. Zelenko indicate that Mr. Knobel was aware of his intentions? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: No. C. LINDER

Q: Okay.
A: He did say that Mark Knobel was the only person he could trust at the time. And, you know, that we should be dealing through Mark Knobel for all things related to him.
03_chunk_0005.title: 03 (chunk 6/11)

03_chunk_0006.text:
Q: Okay. Did Dr. Zelenko indicate that Mr. Knobel was aware of his intentions? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: No. C. LINDER

Q: Okay.
A: He did say that Mark Knobel was the only person he could trust at the time. And, you know, that we should be dealing through Mark Knobel for all things related to him.

Q: And, in fact, you did deal with Mark Knobel on all things related to him. Correct? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: Yes.

Q: Okay. I'm going to represent to you that Mr. Knobel provided testimony at a deposition which took place, I believe, in February. Okay. Mr. Knobel testified specifically that it was not Dr. Zelenko's intention to give Rinat another $2.5 million at the expense of his six oldest children. And that the purpose of the change of beneficiary was merely to accommodate Rinat's desire that -- and Dr. Zelenko's desire that she have money unincumbered by a trust in order to satisfy the mortgage that you were C. LINDER referring to earlier. Do you disagree with Mr. Knobel's testimony? MR. KLINEK: Objection to form. MR. GIELCHINSKY: Objection to form.
A: I'm not sure what, you know, doctor -- the only thing I can say about his intent for the 2.5 was related to the mortgage and Rinat's ability to pay that off rapidly.

Q: Well, isn't his intent also manifested by the irrevocable trust that we spoke about earlier? MR. KLINEK: Form. Object. MR. GIELCHINSKY: Objection to form.
A: I mean, again, we were, you know, going back and forth. We were -- actually, there was a -- a discussion I had with Ben Miller about, you know, allocating specific policies to different trusts at the time because of the -- of the assignment of the 2.5. So, I mean, it doesn't really -- I don't know. His intent, he was, you know, back and forth at the time, and, you C. LINDER know, we didn't have a lot of personal discussion with him at that point when he was in the hospital a few different places, different times. So we didn't, you know, I -- I can't really gauge his complete intent that, you know, shows some, you know, air of intent on leaving certain amounts of percentages in money. But I don't know if, you know, his intent was based upon evaluation of what was left at the time.

Q: Mr. Linder, why would your firm have drafted the -- sorry -- the Family Irrevocable Trust Agreement with Frank Zelenko as trustee, leaving the children and his parents $4.5 million if that was not consistent with Dr. Zelenko's intent? MR. GIELCHINSKY: Form. MR. KLINEK: Objection to form.
A: I mean, we were trying to avoid an estate tax issue with those trusts. That was the primary reason for drafting them. Obviously, we never got to that point. C. LINDER
